title: Recipe executor: disposition of all 117 unresolved findings

scope.outsideScope: Consumers outside this dependency closure and runtime-loaded code are not solved.

accounting.note: Primary actions partition the 117 original rows. Dependencies overlap. These are work items, not 117 independent defects or a claim that any row is now resolved.

conclusion: Use a combination: finish actual integration and correct the Construction protocol; split codec from I/O; improve root/context, private-state, iterator, cancellation and resource models. Impose narrow mechanically checkable boundary/lifetime shapes. Do not ban local mutation, generators, callbacks or dependency injection wholesale.

recommendedRestrictions.rule: Bind operation/job/callback ports at an admitted composition root or through a checked boundary summary; executable inputs must have a declared responsibility/plug. Unknown targets stay non-passing.
Pure encoding modules do not import artifact I/O. Private helpers stay below architectural maps; effectful helpers carry their actual caller’s resource effects.
One active consumer or an explicit exclusive iterator transfer. Finish borrowed mutable-chunk consumption before advancing; copy/take ownership before retention or concurrent use.
File access uses tracked path/handle identities and a proved source borrow/destination permission. Preserve aliases and close/delete effects; a pathname or utility label is not authority.
New unsupported shapes require an influence model or a local rewrite; no assumed-primitive getters or method-name-only exemptions. Private working state remains allowed.

executionOrder.reason: Make the real graph/protocol coherent before treating unresolved injected targets as scanner-only defects.
Separate unused effectful exports and identify actual roots, inputs and callbacks; retain separate whole-module coverage.
Prove private state, suspended/borrowed lifetimes and cancellation value flow without opening blind spots.
Complete symbolic resource/handle proof and group diagnostics, then rerun the same original-ID ledger against a production-root audit.

closurePolicy: Every row remains non-passing until its mechanical proof or source/protocol correction is implemented and re-audited. A source split can remove an unused writer from this execution scope; it does not certify that writer. No agent-review waiver, new map-0 permission, product code change or new test suite is introduced by this review.

actions.title: Connect the real submitted-Bundle entry and bind its ports
actions.decision: Finish production integration. The factory exists, but no production source imports or calls it. Current CLI/Studio generation still reaches bundle.generateBundle through createBundleGenerationOperations.
implementation: Use the real admitted Runtime command to construct the executor with the actual Bundle recipe state, owned job host and operation-owner implementations. Start one job for the whole submitted graph, after the overlap guard.
Resolve targets and callbacks from that composition; add exact source/hash wire bindings at actual owner crossings. Existing authored wire bindings alone cannot manufacture a call target.

Audit from the production composition entry, including registered worker/extension entries. Keep the old whole-plan route explicit until its replacement is complete; a fixture-only port graph is not deployment evidence.
actions.closure: A public submitted-Bundle operation traverses the actual executor, Bundle authority, native operation owners and one job host; scoped analysis resolves those exact targets and checks their declared plugs. Include partial failure, cancellation, stale publication, overlap refusal and resource settlement in focused execution evidence.

actions.title: Replace the stale Construction query protocol
actions.decision: Correct the executor before connecting it. The toolpath branch calls Construction.query and treats its return as identified output data. Current owner intent and 11.1.8 require the Construction command; 3.6 starts Scheduler, and completed work/schedule arrive through separate result-retention commands.
implementation: Use the actual Construction command and explicit work/schedule value receivers, correlated to this admitted Bundle/job and recipe input identities.
Keep command replies to outcomes and created identities. Populate downstream recipe values from the declared value deliveries, not by renaming query to command while retaining its data return.
Reuse the active generation route’s existing Construction/Scheduler implementation. Do not add a second Runtime scheduling recipe or a permissive query binding.
actions.closure: The graph executor receives exact completed work and qualified schedule on construction-work-results/scheduling-results, preserves partial failure and cancellation, and the scanner checks Construction admission and both result-retention commands separately.

actions.title: Admit typed inputs and trace control/observation callbacks
actions.decision: Replace unconstrained pseudo-JSON inputs with real producer/admission facts and model their callbacks in context. Arbitrary JSON is not a valid model for an AbortSignal or job scope. Keep dependency injection, but make callable inputs traceable.
implementation: Derive signal, progress and commit control from the actual owned job host. Propagate concrete receiver/callback identities through object spread, arrays, optional calls and AbortSignal.any.

Admit supplied snapshots at the owning boundary, or restrict snapshot injection to internal use with a proved producer guarantee. Propagate validated Array/data postconditions; do not classify every member named map/query as a platform method.

Remove captured.beforeCommit from the production run-input surface unless an explicit, necessary hook contract is established. The owned job scope already supplies commit control; swallowing observer errors does not remove observer effects.
Model parameterized helpers from validated boundary summaries where callers are intentionally outside scope. Keep genuinely unknown callback targets non-passing.
actions.closure: Each input can be traced to an admitted producer or a mechanically checked boundary summary; every invoked callback retains its actual originating/receiving owners. A callback that activates an undeclared owner still fails.

actions.title: Model cancellation reason as arbitrary data, including exceptional flow
actions.decision: Improve the platform model, not the source getter. AbortSignal.reason may be any JavaScript value, including a callable or an object retaining another owner’s state. It cannot be declared primitive.
implementation: Keep the reason on the concrete signal instance. Model AbortController.abort(reason), AbortSignal.abort(reason), AbortSignal.any source reasons and timeout/default errors.
Propagate reason through property access, explicit throw, throwIfAborted and catch/exceptional flow. Preserve nested aliases and callable identity.

Read declared instance state without executing a native getter against its prototype. If the analyzer cannot represent the exceptional value flow, emit a specific unresolved finding instead of returning an empty primitive.
actions.closure: Reason values and nested/callable aliases survive abort/any/throw/catch paths; primitive reasons stay primitive. Unknown supplied signals remain unresolved rather than inheriting a blanket exemption.

actions.title: Separate callable reachability, declaration templates and real external roots
actions.decision: Improve root selection and parameterized summaries. An ESM export is not automatically a public entry, and an unused generic declaration is not another runtime caller. Keep a separate whole-module ownership inventory.
implementation: Start an execution audit from declared command/worker/manifest entries and follow actual calls, values, initialization effects and escaped callbacks. Preserve a separate module-wide coverage report so unused exports are not silently certified.
Keep call-site copies and closure environments distinct. Do not report an unsupplied declaration template as an actual invocation when all reachable invocations have concrete receivers.

Support checked summaries for reusable helpers with arbitrary data inputs; distinguish this from an open entry that can receive executable callbacks or shared aliases. Include real callers when proving a caller-specific property.
For recipe-only review, split the pure encoder from file I/O (A06) as a direct source-shape improvement; reachability alone must never discard initialization effects or dynamic entry points.
actions.closure: Known Map/Array/callback sites resolve in their actual contexts; unused exports are explicitly inventoried outside the execution certificate. Unknown dynamic loaders, public entries and escaped callbacks remain blockers.
authority: Current operation catalog and extension/worker manifests

actions.title: Separate the codec from artifact I/O and assign responsibility honestly
actions.decision: Split pure JSON/text encoding from effectful artifact writes/copies. Importing jsonChunks should not require solving unrelated file writers. Record pure helpers as utilities after checking isolation; keep filesystem effects attributed to their invoking owner.
implementation: Move jsonChunks/stringPieces/textChunks into an encoding-only module; preserve surrogate handling, finite streaming and negative-zero behavior in recipeDataChunks. Keep required byte-chunk sizes with their implementation or a pure constant module.

Give artifact publication/capture code the existing meaningful responsibility it implements. Generic write mechanics may remain context-sensitive utilities, but their fs contacts must be checked in each caller; a utility label grants no world-channel permission.

Do not assign the mixed current module wholesale to part-generation or observations: Bundle persistence and observation capture are different callers. Keep cleanup callbacks under their enclosing effect owner.
Update imports/re-exports and implementation fingerprints together. No new architecture box is needed for every encoder, loop or hash.
actions.closure: The recipe dependency closure contains the codec without unused writers; retained artifact I/O is separately covered by its actual persistence/capture contexts, resource identities and exact contracts.

actions.title: Model filesystem identities, open modes and handle lifetimes
actions.decision: Improve symbolic resource provenance and contact classification. All eleven contacts have unresolved paths; open-for-read and descriptor close are additionally mislabeled as file-content writes.
implementation: Carry symbolic pathname identity from actual caller arguments through temp-name derivation, open, numeric descriptors and FileHandle methods. Unify descriptor aliases and account for rename/unlink and path aliases; do not require literal filenames.

Distinguish content reads/writes, create/delete/rename and descriptor lifecycle. Interpret open flags; readSync also mutates its destination buffer, and close can interfere with a shared handle even though it writes no file bytes.

Prove exclusive destination creation and a source borrow/lease through real callers. Keep possible shared-file contacts non-passing when alias/lifetime evidence is missing; do not suppress all contacts with path *.
actions.closure: Symbolic same-resource writer/reader and shared-handle close paths are detected; read-only open is not a content write, distinct proved resources remain separate, and source/destination permissions and lifetime follow the actual owner.

actions.title: Prove invocation-private state and completed fresh publication
actions.decision: Treat private working state as private after a lifetime/escape proof. These reports concern local cycle/duplicate sets, a validation RegExp, construction arrays, hashes and ordinary local counters. D-047 already excludes private working state from observable effects.
implementation: Track allocation and lexical activation identity through synchronous calls and recursion; distinguish a fresh default Set from a caller-supplied shared Set.

Allow a synchronous helper to build and publish a fresh result when construction finishes before exposure and no writer is retained. Preserve aliases to nested source data unless actual copying/admission proves otherwise.

For async helpers, retain state per activation across await and prove it is neither exposed nor shared; do not merge all same-source activations or infer privacy just because writer and reader names match.
Retained closure cells, module/platform state and escaping/shared allocations continue to require owner context and transfer proof. Use A09 for suspended generators and A10 for OS handles.
actions.closure: Private helpers can be checked without an artificial architectural owner for every local; a module-retained object, shared closure or caller-supplied mutable accumulator still exposes its cross-owner path.
authority: D-047: private caches and own working state are not effects

actions.title: Model iterator activation and bounded borrowing of chunks
actions.decision: Keep streaming generators; model their suspended state and consumer-driven execution. For mutable chunks, impose a narrow borrow rule: finish consumption before advancing the producer, or copy/take ownership before retention or concurrent use.
implementation: Represent generator creation separately from next/return/throw and for-of/yield* activation. Propagate the consumer’s call context to resumed effects and preserve per-iterator lexical/storage identity.
Prove a single active consumer or explicit exclusive handoff of each iterator. Shared iterator state across owners remains visible, even if the generator has no global variables.

byteChunks yields slices/full buffers and replaces completed buffers; keep Buffer views tied to their actual backing stores. copyArtifactSync/chunks reuses its read buffer, so downstream byteChunks must finish its read/copy before the next readSync.

Verify the synchronous writer finishes each chunk before the next advance and the async writer awaits writeFile before advancing. Retaining/queuing a borrowed slice beyond the next advance requires a copy or an explicit immutable ownership transfer.
Until activation/alias lifetime is modeled, keep these findings open. Do not waive all generator locals or replace bounded streaming with a whole-document copy.
actions.closure: Fresh and delegated iterators retain precise consumers and effects; supported chunk borrowing verifies, while retained mutable views, two consumers and cross-owner resumed work cannot pass silently.

actions.title: Keep FileHandle identity separate from file-content authority
actions.decision: A locally created FileHandle is a private wrapper around an external resource. Proving the wrapper private does not prove its file is private. Model both identities.
implementation: Preserve open-produced handle identity and its pathname/flags across await, writeFile, close and cleanup.
Prove the handle does not escape; attribute each file contact to the owner/resource permission in A07. Keep cleanup/close ordering in the lifetime summary.
actions.closure: Local handle state stops creating spurious shared-heap alarms while file access and shared-handle invalidation remain checked.

actions.title: Group repeated source findings without losing invocation evidence
actions.decision: Improve presentation, preserving the solve. IDs 114–117 repeat the same source cells as 106–109 under another analyzer copy. They are not four additional design defects.
implementation: Use a stable source-cell identity for the primary finding and list each distinct invocation/owner context as evidence beneath it.
Deduplicate identical origin/reason pairs, but retain different owners, aliases and lifetimes. A reporting merge cannot turn an unresolved context into a pass.
actions.closure: One source finding links all invocation evidence, including copies that genuinely differ in owner context; no non-passing path is discarded.

findings.decision: Classify close separately, preserving handle alias/lifetime influence and resource provenance.
findings.closure: No spurious content write is emitted; closing another consumer’s shared handle still creates a checked interaction.

findings.subject: Failure cleanup close
findings.diagnosis: Same lifecycle issue as ID 46, in the error path.
findings.decision: Keep the error-path close tied to the same fd and owner, without counting it as writing file bytes.
findings.closure: Cleanup invalidation is modeled even when writing or hashing throws.

findings.subject: Failure cleanup unlink
findings.diagnosis: Deletes only after this invocation created the destination. It is a real filesystem mutation.
findings.decision: Retain delete/namespace contact, path provenance and created-state control through failure cleanup.
findings.closure: Delete targets the owned created file, or uncertainty remains explicit.

findings.subject: Async exclusive destination open
findings.diagnosis: fs/promises.open(file,wx) returns a FileHandle after await; current contact path is unknown.

findings.closure: Handle and destination identities survive await; creation effect remains checked.

findings.subject: Async FileHandle write
findings.diagnosis: FileHandle.writeFile has the destination on its receiver, not in its first argument (the chunk).
findings.decision: Derive resource provenance from the resolved handle receiver and keep chunk borrowing until write completion.
findings.closure: The contact refers to the opened file, never the chunk as a filename; actual writes/aliases remain checked.

findings.subject: Async cleanup unlink
findings.diagnosis: A real delete of the invocation-created target after failure; no caller path is present in this scope.
findings.decision: Carry symbolic file identity/created condition through cleanup and suppressed cleanup failures.
findings.closure: The real delete permission is checked regardless of the catch handler returning nothing.

findings.subject: Read-only source open
findings.diagnosis: openSync(file,r) is currently labeled file-write because its model advertises an undifferentiated fs effect. This classification is wrong.
findings.decision: Interpret the r flags: source read capability plus descriptor lifecycle, with a borrow interval; do not erase source reads.
findings.closure: Read-only open is not a content write; the actual source identity and borrow remain required.

findings.subject: Source close
findings.diagnosis: Read-source fd is closed in finally; scanner again labels it a file-content write.
findings.decision: Model source-handle invalidation and caller borrow end, including exceptional completion.
findings.closure: No invented content write; early shared-handle invalidation still cannot pass silently.

findings.subject: Chunked source read
findings.diagnosis: readSync uses fd from the outer copy function and mutates a reused Buffer before yielding a view.
findings.decision: Follow the captured fd back to the source path and model destination buffer storage plus borrow timing (A09).
findings.closure: Source content reads and buffer mutation/alias lifetime are both attributed correctly.
